rules.law_name: An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.title: Proposed statewide rent-control cap blocked from November 2026 ballot
rules.requirement: The blocked initiative would have capped annual rent increases for most Massachusetts residential rental units at the lesser of CPI or 5%. It would have exempted certain owner-occupied, newly constructed, publicly regulated, short-term, educational, religious, and nonprofit facilities.
rules.key_value: lesser of annual CPI increase or 5%

coverage.other_unresolvable: Exemptions for certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
coverage.summary: Would have applied to most residential rental units in Massachusetts, with stated exemptions including owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units and newly constructed units less than 10 years old.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
rules.interaction: The petition would have repealed Massachusetts’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, but the SJC ruled it could not appear on the November 2026 ballot because of its religious exemption.
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%. rules.title: Massachusetts statutory ban on rent control
rules.requirement: Massachusetts law contains a statutory ban on rent control. Local rent-control limits are barred unless the state law is changed or repealed.

coverage.summary: Applies statewide as a ban on rent control.

rules.interaction: The blocked Initiative Petition 25-21 would have repealed this statutory ban and replaced it with a statewide annual rent-increase cap.
rules.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases for most residential rental units.
